articles.title: 三星携手 Reality Defender，面向新加坡企业用户开发端侧 AI 深度伪造检测方案
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，三星宣布联合深度伪造检测公司 Reality Defender 合作，开发面向企业用户的端侧 AI 深度伪造检测方案。该方案将直接在三星 Galaxy 设备上运行，帮助企业识别 AI 生成的虚假语音、视频和图像，降低冒充诈骗及其他相关风险，计划率先落地新加坡市场。IT之家获悉，Reality Defender 专注于企业级深度伪造检测，利用多种 AI 模型实时分析语音、视频和图像内容。例如，该技术能够在实时通话中识别冒充他人的合成语音，也可用于客户身份识别和新用户注册审核，帮助企业发现可疑的虚假内容。Reality Defender 表示，随着生成式 AI 技术的发展，利用合成语音和视频实施诈骗的情况日益受到关注。有调查显示，2024 年新加坡有 56% 的企业曾遭遇音频深度伪造诈骗，另有 52% 的企业遇到过视频深度伪造相关事件。个人用户同样面临此类诈骗带来的经济损失。数据显示，2025 年，新加坡受冒充政府官员诈骗影响的受害者至少损失 2.429 亿新元），占当地全年诈骗总损失的 26.6%。三星电子新加坡公司综合业务部门总监兼负责人 Timothy Tan 表示，三星希望通过此次合作，帮助企业更早发现潜在威胁，双方计划开发实用的端侧深度伪造检测方案，在相关数据需要上传至云端处理之前，就能识别潜在风险。此次合作的一大重点是将检测过程放在 Galaxy 设备本地完成。与依赖云端分析的方案相比，这种方式有望减少敏感数据向外部服务器传输的需求，从而降低数据泄露风险。三星还计划借助 Knox 安全平台，为相关功能提供保护。Knox 覆盖从芯片底层到应用层的多个安全环节。目前，三星尚未公布这套方案的具体上线时间，也没有透露哪些 Galaxy 机型将获得支持。目前来看相应项目主要面向新加坡企业用户，未来有望率先帮助当地企业避免 AI 诈骗风险。

articles.title: 【IT之家开箱】微星神影 16 魔龙姬星际套装图赏：星云白 + 魔龙姬，这套装备有点特别
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，作为微星 40 周年推出的特别之作，神影 16 魔龙姬限定款把二次元 IP「魔龙姬」融进了传统的游戏本里，用一抹星云白取代常见的黑色机身，让这台高性能机器多了一份清爽与个性。目前IT之家已经拿到了这款特别的游戏本新品 —— 神影 16 魔龙姬星际套装 2026。值得一提的是，本次IT之家拿到的并不只有笔记本本体，还包括同主题耳机、鼠标和鼠标垫。从机身到外设，整套装备都融入了魔龙姬的设计元素，视觉风格保持统一。设计上，微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款采用了星云白配色，并将微星旗下的二次元 IP「魔龙姬」融入整体设计。机身 A 面采用白色盖板，右侧布置了微星龙盾 Logo。表面的幻彩珠光涂层会随着光线和观察角度的变化，呈现出细微的色泽差异，让纯白机身多了几分层次感。整体线条依然保留了游戏本应有的硬朗感，而星云白配色则柔和了传统电竞设计的凌厉气质，让整机看起来更加清爽，也少了几分张扬。微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款可以单手掀开屏幕，最大开合角度约为 135°。翻开机身，其配备了一块 16 英寸釉月屏，屏幕上边框中央集成了摄像头，旁边设置了物理防窥开关，并配有麦克风开孔。分辨率为 2560×1600（2.5K），16:10 比例，刷新率达到 240Hz，官方标称覆盖 100% DCI-P3 广色域、500nits 峰值亮度。C 面的键盘区域延续了白色主题，采用带数字小键盘的全尺寸布局，下方搭配一块大尺寸一体式触控板。WASD 四个按键与电源键使用了半透明键帽设计，方便背光透出。方向键则加入了像素风格的网点渐变纹理，与魔龙姬限定版的个性化设计相呼应。触控板采用与机身一致的白色设计，表面略微下凹，横向延伸的布局也让整个掌托区域看起来更加舒展。机身尺寸方面，微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款厚度约为 21.95–23.85mm，重量约 2.25kg。相比上一代产品，这次全新模具在体积上做了明显瘦身，配合白色机身，视觉上比传统厚重游戏本轻盈不少。接口布局上，微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款将接口分布在机身左右两侧及后部。机身左侧设有锁孔、电源接口，以及两个 USB-C 接口，均支持最高 10Gbps 数据传输，并支持 100W PD 供电和 DP 1.4 视频输出。机身右侧提供一个 3.5mm 二合一音频接口，以及两个支持 5Gbps 传输速率的 USB-A 接口。后部则安排了 RJ45 有线网口、HDMI 2.1 FRL 接口和一个 5Gbps USB-A 接口。这样的布局覆盖了游戏、外接显示器和常见 USB 外设等使用场景。此外，随机器附带的电源适配器输出功率为 240W，规格为 20V/12A。至于体积，也是意料之内了。翻到机身底部，D 面同样采用星云白配色，不过设计语言与 A 面有所区别。几何线条让底部显得更具机械感，右上角的红色结构件则增加了视觉对比。底部设置了两条较为醒目的大面积进风区域，机身四周和中间分布着防滑脚垫，为桌面放置提供支撑。微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款电池容量为 80Wh。存储方面，机器提供两个 M.2 SSD 插槽，出厂搭载的三星 PM9C1b 固态硬盘容量为 512GB，采用 PCIe 4.0 规格，旁边还预留了一个支持 PCIe 5.0 的 M.2 插槽。性能部分，微星神影 16 魔龙姬星际套装，核心配置和之前的锐龙版保持一致：搭载 AMD 锐龙 9 8940HX 处理器与 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU，115W 满功耗释放。整机双烤功耗可达 190W。配备了酷寒散热系统，采用双风扇、五热管、四出风口的散热模组布局，覆盖 CPU 与 GPU 两大核心热源。京东微星（MSI）微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定版 游戏本电竞笔记本电脑【国家补贴】智能体 可扩容内存硬盘高刷 16 英寸 【魔龙姬星际套装】R9-8940HX 丨满血 5060 丨 16G 512G9999 元直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 15999 元起，苹果首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo 开启预购
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，苹果首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo 将于今晚 8 点开启预购，国行定价 15999 元起，IT之家整理价格如下：256GB 版：15999 元512GB 版：17999 元1TB 版：21499 元2TB 版：26499 元京东苹果 iPhone Duo 手机 15999 元起直达链接该机提供星光白和夜空双色可选，提供 IP68 认证，屏幕方面采用四边一致的窄边框设计。手机内外屏拥有统一显示比例，手机内外屏均支持 Apple Pencil（今年晚些时候），其中内屏规格为 7.6 英寸 1878 x 2670 分辨率 120Hz（采用屏下摄像头），外屏规格为 5.4 英寸 1398 x 2034 分辨率 120Hz，两块屏幕均支持全天候显示，以及最高 3000 尼特的户外峰值亮度。该机机身边框由航空级钛金属打造，使用侧边指纹，铰链机构采用定制的可变扭矩设计，拥有超 100 个部件，展开状态下厚度 5.2mm，是迄今为止最薄的 iPhone。机身顶部和底部均提供扬声器，具有较佳的音频效果。该机搭载 A20 Pro 处理器，拥有大尺寸 VC 均热板，号称相对 iPhone 17 Pro 持续性能提升 35%。手机全球版本均采用 eSIM 设计，匹配 C2 基带芯片，相比 C1X 速度提升 50%，能耗降低 15%，在软硬件加持下，手机充满一次电续航至高 24 小时，使用外屏播放视频提供至高 44 小时续航，手机充电 5 分钟可在外屏上观看 5 小时视频。该机前置 12Mp 自拍摄像头，背面搭载 48Mp 主摄及 48Mp 融合式超广角，支持拍摄 4K 杜比视界 HDR 视频，提供全新“智能拍摄”功能，不需要用户动手按快门即可自动拍摄。软件方面，该机充分利用大屏空间，主屏幕上的程序坞采用竖向布局，控制项放在了方便拇指操作的位置。手机支持同时操作两个应用，支持半折叠使用，可秒变日历、闹钟、桌面音箱。京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 社交平台 Bluesky 扩展旗下 Attie AI 工具功能：支持创建小游戏、投票等社交应用
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，社交平台 Bluesky 宣布扩展旗下 AI 工具 Attie，用户现在可以通过输入提示词，创建小游戏、投票和数据仪表盘等轻量级社交应用，并将其作为独立网站分享给其他人。Bluesky 首席执行官 Toni Schneider 表示，如今的 Attie 能实现“面向社区的氛围编程”，用户无需编写大量代码，只需描述自己的想法，就能快速创建供社区成员使用的应用。目前，Attie 官方网站已经展示了多个示例，包括模仿《Flappy Bird》的“Flappy Butterfly”小游戏、鼓机、问答游戏，以及以芹菜人为主题的放置点击游戏。每款应用都会获得一个位于 attie.site 域名下的独立链接，页面底部还会标注创建者信息，方便用户分享作品并了解应用的制作者。不过，从目前的实际体验来看，Attie 生成的应用大多仍属于功能较为简单的轻量级作品，娱乐性和新鲜感较强，后续 Attie 能否发展为更成熟的氛围编程创作社交平台，还有待观察。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，华硕 ROG 超杀 27 二代显示器今晚 20:00 开售，到手价 3299 元。这款显示器搭载了一块 26.5 英寸 2K 320Hz QD-OLED 面板；采用 BlackShield 黑盾涂层，相比前代抗刮擦能力提升至 2.5 倍；拥有 1.5M:1 对比度、 0.03ms GTG 响应时间、 99% DCI-P3 色域、Delta E<2 色准，通过 VESA DisplayHDR 500 认证。这款显示器背部搭载标志性 ROG 标识，顶部配有三脚架插孔，方便直播搭载相机；配备人体工学支架，支持 0~110mm 高低调整、 -45°~+45° 水平旋转、 -5°~+20° 前后倾斜、 -90°~+90° 垂直旋转。IT之家获悉，这款显示器配备一个 DisplayPort 1.4 接口（支持 DSC 影像压缩传输）、一个 HDMI 2.1 接口，以及一个支持 15W PD 输出的 USB-C 接口。京东华硕 ROG 超杀 27 二代 3299 元直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 长安汽车高层人事调整，赵非接替朱华荣任董事长
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，长安汽车今日公告称，朱华荣申请辞去公司董事长、董事、法定代表人职务，不再代行公司董事会秘书职责，不再担任公司及控股子公司任何职务。朱华荣继续担任中国长安汽车集团有限公司（以下简称“中国长安汽车”）党委书记、董事长，从集团层面统筹旗下汽车业务的整体规划和长远发展。▲ 朱华荣IT之家注意到，董事会选举赵非为公司董事长、法定代表人，董事长任期自本次董事会会议审议通过之日起至第十届董事会任期届满之日止，不再担任公司总裁。在董事会未聘任董事会秘书期间，由董事长代行董事会秘书职责。董事会聘任叶沛为公司总裁，不再担任公司常务执行副总裁，聘任杨大勇为公司常务执行副总裁，不再担任公司执行副总裁，聘任邓承浩为公司执行副总裁，不再担任公司副总裁。▲ 赵非长安汽车表示，本次调整旨在充分发挥中国长安汽车作为专业化汽车产业集团“定战略、配资源、促协同、控风险、强激励”的作用，有利于公司进一步优化市场化机制、聚焦全球化经营，推动上市公司高质量发展。公告同时肯定了朱华荣任职期间的工作。朱华荣在任职期间，领导推动长安汽车第三次创业-创新创业计划，推进新能源“香格里拉”、智能化“北斗天枢”、全球化“海纳百川”战略布局，打造阿维塔、深蓝、启源等品牌，推动公司向智能低碳出行科技公司转型，为公司高质量发展做出重大贡献，董事会对朱华荣先生在任职期间的勤勉尽责工作表示衷心感谢。

articles.title: XREAL One Pro Plus 智能眼镜发布：峰值亮度提升至 1200 尼特、鼻托结构重新设计，599 美元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，XREAL 今日在海外发布新款 AR 眼镜 Xreal One Pro Plus，主要提升面板亮度，同时调整人体工程学设计，定价为 599 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 4,015 元人民币）。Xreal One Pro Plus 采用重新设计的鼻托结构，旨在改善眼镜与面部的贴合度，提升长时间观看时的舒适性。其搭载双 0.55 英寸索尼 Micro-OLED 面板，峰值亮度最高可达 1200 尼特，较前代产品的 700 尼特明显提升。除了更高的峰值亮度，新品还加入 AI HDR 功能，借助 AI 技术改善画面对比度，让用户通过眼镜观看内容时获得更好的视觉体验。同时眼镜新增标准、电影和阅读三种显示模式，用户可以根据日常使用、观看影片或阅读等不同场景选择合适的显示效果。XREAL 表示，新款眼镜还改进了内置的 Real 3D 引擎，可将普通 2D 内容转换为具有空间感的 3D 画面，处理帧率最高提升至 60 FPS，新品的其他核心硬件变化不大，仍搭载 Xreal 自研的 X1 空间计算芯片，视场角也维持在 57 度，与上一代产品相同。

articles.title: 四部门组织 30 余家车企座谈：加强汽车研发测试验证管理，明确产品宣传红线
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据央视新闻报道，工业和信息化部、公安部、生态环境部、市场监管总局四部门组织 30 余家重点汽车生产企业开展座谈，加强汽车产品创新设计和研发测试验证管理。四部门在会上明确要求汽车生产企业落实质量提升专项行动工作要求，坚决抵制非理性竞争，守牢产品安全底线。此次座谈会对汽车生产企业提出了两方面重点要求。一是全面加强测试验证，增强研发测试验证能力，充分开展产品创新设计安全评估和研发测试验证，及时消除安全隐患。二是如实宣传产品创新设计的使用边界、限制条件和研发测试验证等情况，不得作虚假、夸大或引人误解的宣传，不得使用违反道路交通法规的场景来宣传产品功能，不得诱导驾驶人忽视安全驾驶责任。工业和信息化部表示，下一步将加快推进有关标准制修订，进一步提升安全基线要求，对重点汽车生产企业持续开展监督检查，依法依规严肃处理存在问题的生产企业并向社会公开曝光。IT之家注意到，此次座谈并非今年监管部门围绕汽车安全与质量问题的首次行动。10 月 10 日，四部门联合发布了《关于进一步加强汽车产品创新设计和研发测试验证有关管理工作的通知（征求意见稿）》，对汽车制动系统等关键结构件、可靠性与耐久性验证以及隐藏式门把手、零重力座椅等创新设计提出了明确要求。该征求意见稿新增 51 项车辆产品主要技术参数，其中 41 项针对产品创新设计，10 项针对产品研发测试验证。在研发测试验证方面，征求意见稿要求新申报产品必须完成综合可靠性与耐久性、结构可靠性、软件功能可靠性等测试，环境适应性验证周期不少于 1 年且须包含“两冬一夏”试验，可靠性验证试验里程不低于 3 万公里。在创新设计方面，征求意见稿列出了明确的禁止性条款，包括禁止配备全隐藏式车门把手，行车过程中不得使用“零重力”座椅、旋转座椅或座椅放倒成床等功能，应急逃生和应急制动等涉及安全的操纵件必须保留实体操纵件和醒目标识。征求意见稿发布后，多家车企政策研究部门在周末即启动专题学习，逐条梳理文件要求，后续还将组织研发、产品、测试等多部门开展全员传达与研讨，对照新规要求自查现有车型开发流程，评估后续新品规划的调整方向。受访企业和专家普遍认为，此次监管精准纠偏行业“重创新噱头、轻安全验证”的乱象，倒逼产业告别快消式造车逻辑。更早的 8 月 27 日，四部门已联合发布通知，在全国范围内启动为期 1 年的道路机动车辆产品生产一致性和质量提升专项行动，集中整治生产一致性、可靠性、耐久性、新技术测试验证等四方面问题。延伸阅读此次座谈是四部门正在开展的“道路机动车辆产品生产一致性和质量提升专项行动”的一部分。2026 年 8 月 27 日，工业和信息化部、公安部、生态环境部、市场监管总局联合发布通知，决定自即日起在全国范围内开展为期 1 年的道路机动车辆产品生产一致性和质量提升专项行动。该专项行动集中整治四方面问题：生产一致性、可靠性、耐久性以及新技术测试验证。其中“新技术测试验证”就包括产品组合驾驶辅助及自动驾驶功能测试验证是否充分，产品及云端平台数据安全、网络安全防护是否充分，以及营销宣传是否符合实际情况等。在本次座谈之前，相关部署已多次展开。2026 年 7 月 17 日，工业和信息化部装备工业一司组织召开重点汽车生产企业座谈会，要求车企坚决抵制非理性竞争，加强产品测试验证与安全评估，不得夸大和虚假宣传。2026 年 9 月 24 日前后，四部门相关司局又组织重点货车、客车、专用车、挂车及摩托车生产企业开展座谈；此前还组织过重点乘用车生产企业开展座谈。在标准层面，2026 年 7 月 2 日，《智能网联汽车组合驾驶辅助系统安全要求》（GB 47955—2026）强制性国家标准由国家市场监督管理总局、国家标准化管理委员会批准发布，拟于 2027 年 1 月 1 日起正式实施。该标准立足系统“辅助”驾驶这一核心定位，从功能要求、数据记录、车辆制造商安全保障等维度提出安全运行基线要求，并针对基础单车道、基础多车道、领航驾驶辅助等三类产品分别提出适用要求。文中提到的“辅助驾驶”与“自动驾驶”在国标中有明确区分。根据《汽车驾驶自动化分级》（GB/T 40429—2021），驾驶自动化分为 L0 至 L5 共 6 个等级，其中 L0—L2 级属于组合驾驶辅助，人类驾驶人始终是驾驶主体并承担安全第一责任；L3—L5 级才属于自动驾驶。目前市面绝大多数量产乘用车搭载的均为 L2 级辅助驾驶系统。针对宣传用语的规范此前已有动作。2025 年 4 月 16 日，工业和信息化部装备工业一司召开智能网联汽车产品准入及软件在线升级管理工作推进会，强调车企不得进行夸大和虚假宣传，严格履行告知义务；据参会车企人士透露，细则要求不能出现“自动驾驶”“自主驾驶”“智驾”“高阶智驾”等名词，应按自动化分级标准使用“（组合）辅助

articles.title: 上海市委书记陈吉宁会见美国苹果公司执行董事长蒂姆 · 库克
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据“上海发布”公众号，上海市委书记陈吉宁今天（10 月 16 日）会见了美国苹果公司执行董事长蒂姆 · 库克一行。陈吉宁提到，当前，新一轮科技革命和产业变革加速突破，人工智能技术和产业发展突飞猛进，为包括苹果公司在内的全球企业在沪发展带来新的机遇。欢迎用好上海的改革开放优势、科技创新优势和市场渠道优势，围绕智能终端供给、创新生态培育、人工智能健康发展等深化交流合作，推动更多新产品、新技术、新服务落地上海。上海将持续优化市场化、法治化、国际化一流营商环境，加快完善与高水平开放相适应的监管体系和法律体系，支持全球企业在沪实现更好发展。蒂姆 · 库克表示，每次来到上海这座全球卓越城市，都能感受到蓬勃发展的活力和科技创新的动力。十分高兴在这里看到人工智能技术赋能千行百业的新实践新探索，愿持续深耕上海，携手合作伙伴围绕人工智能发展、产业生态构建、供应链管理、绿色低碳转型等加强对接、深化合作，在推动美中经贸关系稳定健康发展中发挥好工商界的桥梁纽带作用，更好实现互利共赢发展。IT之家注意到，苹果董事会执行主席蒂姆 · 库克近日开启中国之行，到访广州、北京、上海等城市。10 月 15 日，商务部部长王文涛会见苹果公司执行董事长蒂姆 · 库克。双方就中美经贸关系、人工智能发展、苹果公司在华业务等议题进行交流。相关阅读：《库克卸任 CEO 后首次来华：首站落地广州，观看苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 手机拍摄的非遗咏春作品》《广东省省长孟凡利会见苹果执行董事长库克一行，库克称愿意进一步扩大在粤业务布局》《库克分享卸任苹果 CEO 后首次来华最新动态：与苏炳添喝早茶聊天、同 Xmind 思维导图开发者交流等》《苹果库克现身清华大学：参加经管学院顾问委员会年会，目前担任主席》《苹果库克现身爱奇艺总部，爱奇艺 CEO 龚宇亲自接待》《苹果库克、腾讯马化腾、百度李彦宏登上〈新闻联播〉，参加清华经管学院顾问委员会 2026 年会》《商务部部长王文涛会见美国苹果公司执行董事长蒂姆 · 库克，就人工智能发展等进行交流》《苹果库克时隔 3 年再次现身米哈游总部，与“大伟哥”见面》

articles.title: Pimco’s Balls Sees Good Value in Long End of Yield Curve
articles.content: Andrew Balls, global fixed income CIO at Pimco, says one to two further interest-rate hikes from the Federal Reserve “seems reasonable” as the central bank targets a return to 2% inflation. He also explains why he sees “good value” in the long end of the Treasury yield curve amid uncertainty around artificial intelligence. He speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 索尼撤回对 Xperia 10 VI 的系统更新承诺，原定三次大版本更新改为两次
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，索尼昨日在官网发布公告，确认 Xperia 10 VI 将不会获得 Android 17 更新。索尼承认这一决定与最初的承诺不符，并向用户致歉。索尼表示，该机型在发布时曾承诺提供三次 Android 系统大版本更新，但经过详细技术评估后，由于设备存储配置的限制，Xperia 10 VI 无法支持符合索尼标准的 Android 17 升级体验，因此决定不提供此次更新。索尼于上月开始向旗舰机型 Xperia 1 VIII 推送 Android 17，同时公布了一份符合条件的机型列表，Xperia 10 VI 并不在其中，这引发了外界对该机型更新计划的疑虑。TI 之家注：Xperia 10 VI 于 2024 年发布，搭载高通骁龙 6 Gen 1 芯片，配备 8GB 内存和 128GB 存储，出厂预装 Android 14。按照索尼的更新计划，该机已于 2025 年 2 月升级至 Android 15，2025 年 10 月升级至 Android 16，Android 17 本应是其最后一次大版本更新。Android Authority 指出，索尼提到的“存储配置限制”具体指向何种技术问题尚不明确，索尼从未说明该机采用的是 UFS 2.2 还是其他类型的存储。不过，获得 Android 17 更新的 Xperia 10 VII 同样配备 128GB 存储，而其他厂商搭载 UFS 2.2 存储的多款设备也将推送 Android 17 更新。索尼在公告中强调，该问题仅涉及 Xperia 10 VI 的技术规格，不会影响其他 Xperia 机型。安全更新承诺保持不变，索尼将继续为 Xperia 10 VI 提供自产品发布之日起四年的安全更新。按此计算，安全更新将持续至 2028 年 5 月。

articles.title: 爱优腾集齐 + 体验对齐：鸿蒙华为视频 App 获 1.2.30.301 版本升级，看爱奇艺再不用“跳端”
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，鸿蒙华为视频 App（手机桌面、应用市场显示为“视频”）今日开启了 1.2.30.301 版本升级，其更新日志显示为集齐了“爱优腾芒”四大平台。鸿蒙华为视频 App 此次更新日志如下：1、App 内直接观看爱奇艺内容，无需跳端，追剧更丝滑（手机 / pad）；2、推荐栏目新增影片 AI 推荐语，快速读懂剧集，选片更精准（手机 / pad）；3、汇聚爱优腾芒四大平台，精品热播内容已上新。事实上，去年 11 月，鸿蒙华为视频 App 在更新 1.1.10.300 版本后，就放开了爱奇艺账号绑定和视频专区，用户可直接在 App 内播放爱奇艺的独家版权内容。但用户在此前版本观看爱奇艺内容，会多一道步骤 —— 播放内容时会跳转至爱奇艺小程序。IT之家实测，最新版华为视频虽然也是在小程序内播放，但体验得到了优化：点击爱奇艺内容后不会再有前往小程序的割裂跳转动画，而是采用类似开启 App 内二级页面的自然过渡动画（后台也不会显示爱奇艺小程序进程），进一步对齐了其他平台体验。▲ 图源：华为视频爱奇艺专区播放视频截图其他平台内容，如腾讯视频、优酷视频，其体验会更加原生化，顶端不会再显示小程序的开关、设置按钮，而是会提供投播、小窗、定时关闭等功能入口。▲ 图源：华为视频腾讯视频专区播放视频截图另外，华为视频还引入了央视频专区，点击任意内容会跳转至“央视频精选”小程序。值得一提的是，在“央视频精选”小程序内可免费观看大部分 CCTV 和卫视频道（4K 内容需付费，且需要在央视频 App 内观看。）

articles.title: 手握“HyperHybrid 增程技术”的奥地利集团 Obrist 破产：曾为特斯拉汽车“电改增程”
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据外媒 electrek 报道，为特斯拉汽车“电改增程”而闻名的奥地利集团 Obrist 已陷入破产，其旗下 3 家公司目前均已资不抵债，合计负债约 3,180 万欧元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2.39 亿元人民币）。过去十余年间，该公司一直在推广名为 HyperHybrid 的增程技术，试图将其打造为纯电动汽车的替代方案，但最终未能推出任何量产车型。其中，负责 HyperHybrid 动力系统的 Obrist Powertrain 欠 34 名债权人约 1,885 万欧元（现汇率约合 1.42 亿元人民币），目前仅剩 9 名员工。持有集团甲醇生产和二氧化碳捕集相关专利的 Obrist Technologies 则欠 10 名债权人约 608 万欧元（现汇率约合 4,565.7 万元人民币），已经没有员工。集团旗下负责德国销售和研发业务的 Obrist DE 同样陷入资不抵债，负债约 680 万欧元（现汇率约合 5,106.4 万元人民币）。创始人 Frank Obrist 将公司陷入困境归因于多年高昂的研发成本、未能成功的投资者谈判，以及欧洲汽车行业面临的危机。AKV 还指出，欧洲汽车制造商逐步转向纯电动汽车，也是导致集团破产的原因之一。Obrist 最早于 2020 年初引起关注，当时公司发布了一款基于特斯拉 Model 3 改造的原型车“Mark II”。该车将原有电池组容量缩减至 17.3 kWh，并在前备厢内安装了一台功率为 40 kW 的双缸汽油发电机，宣称综合续航里程可达 1000 公里。当时，Obrist 声称已经将这套动力系统授权给一家未具名的“国际合作伙伴”，并预计搭载该系统的量产车型将在 2023 年前推出。公司还表示，随着产量提升，这套系统的成本可控制在约 4,500 欧元（现汇率约合 33,793 元人民币），并有望将 Model 3 的售价削减一半以上。然而，这家合作伙伴始终没有公开露面，量产车型也从未问世。此后，Obrist 虽多次在欧洲车展上展示相关技术，但始终未能拿出真正投入市场的产品。2022 年，Obrist 又推出了一款基于特斯拉 Model Y 的原型车，改用其称为“aFuel”的合成甲醇作为燃料，并将宣传重点从低成本混合动力转向所谓的“气候正效益”出行。公司声称，这款车每行驶 1 公里就能从大气中移除 24 克二氧化碳，理由是生产燃料时捕集的部分碳最终会被封存于地下。然而 Obrist 始终未能将其技术构想转化为量产产品。该公司的商业模式主要依赖动力系统授权，却始终缺乏能够公开验证的量产客户，同时不断强调纯电动汽车存在缺陷。随着早期承诺未能兑现，其宣传重点又从 2023 年量产计划转向所谓的气候正效益甲醇，最终进一步扩大为取代全球化石燃料、总投资高达 50 万亿美元（现汇率约合 335.15 万亿元人民币）的宏大构想。与此同时，纯电动汽车的电池成本持续下降，续航里程不断提升，Obrist 希望解决的“续航焦虑”问题也在逐渐缓解，种种原因共同导致了其最终迎来破产结局。

articles.title: 泰国警方查获非法跨境光纤：350 米线路直通缅甸电诈园区，每日 6TB 流量相当于 300~400 人使用
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据 Tom's Hardware 今日报道，泰国警方近日在泰缅边境查获一起涉嫌为缅甸诈骗园区非法提供网络服务的案件。据介绍，泰国当局在边境村庄发现一条跨境铺设的 48 芯光纤线缆，长约 350 米，每日传输数据量约为 6TB，疑似用于为缅甸境内的非法赌场及诈骗中心提供网络连接。据《南华早报》报道，执法人员对泰国北碧府 Nong Lu 村的两处民宅展开搜查。该地区毗邻缅甸三佛塔关口，是泰缅边境网络诈骗活动较为集中的区域之一。警方发现，两处普通民宅的网络使用量异常庞大，足以满足整个村庄的日常网络需求。其中一处民宅附近发现了一条带有坚固保护层的 48 芯光纤。线缆沿杆塔铺设，并向缅甸境内延伸约 350 米，涉嫌将泰国的网络带宽跨境输送至相关犯罪场所。泰国国家广播与电信委员会副秘书长兼代理秘书长 Trairat Viriyasirikul 表示，该线路每日使用的数据流量约为 6TB，相当于 300 至 400 人的网络需求。调查人员怀疑，这些网络资源被非法转接至缅甸境内的一处诈骗园区，为当地非法赌场和涉嫌诈骗的场所提供网络连接。报道称，一名身份尚未公开的男性嫌疑人每天收取 700 泰铢（IT之家注：现汇率约合 139.9 元人民币），允许相关人员通过其住所铺设线路。泰缅边境的网络诈骗园区近年来持续受到区域执法部门关注。路透社 2025 年 3 月曾报道称，泰国警方估计，缅甸边境诈骗中心仍有多达 10 万人工作，其中既包括涉嫌参与诈骗的人员，也包括遭人口贩运或胁迫从事诈骗活动的受害者。《南华早报》还指出，随着缅甸境内及柬埔寨部分诈骗园区遭遇打击，一些相关犯罪组织据称正将业务转移至规模较小的酒店、公寓和别墅等场所，而非继续依赖大型集中式园区。相关阅读：《缅甸打击妙瓦底电诈网赌窝点：逮捕 777 人，所缴电脑、手机等设备进行销毁》《公安部：缅甸妙瓦底 KK 园区 630 余栋相关建筑物已被全部拆除，1500 余嫌犯押解回国》《缅甸成立打击电诈网赌中央监督委员会》《纪录片〈缅北电诈覆灭纪实〉今晚 18 点开播，公安部和中央广播电视总台联合摄制》

articles.title: 《战地风云 6》第五赛季部分新皮肤被指 AI 生成：角色装备设计反常、臂章拼错单词
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据外媒 kotaku 报道，《战地风云 6》第五赛季“Siege of Vegas”于本周上线，玩家随即发现本赛季通行证中的一批新角色皮肤疑似存在 AI 制作痕迹。IT之家获悉，其中一名角色的战术背心上挂着大量额外弹匣，另一名角色的装备上竟然同时配有 5 把手枪，还有一名角色的手臂安全臂章将英文单词“Security”（安全）拼成了“Secuty”，同时纹理存在 AI 生图常见的“融合”效果。更令玩家不满的是，这些存在争议的角色外观并非免费内容，而是包含在赛季通行证中。有玩家发帖批评，让玩家花钱购买疑似 AI 生成的内容，是对消费者的不尊重。尽管截至目前开发团队尚未就这些皮肤是否使用生成式 AI 制作作出明确回应，但实际上在去年 12 月时，就有玩家发现本作“寒风”道具包中的贴纸疑似使用 AI 生成，相应贴纸图案描绘出了一把“带有双枪管”的 M4A1 突击步枪。同时，EA 在利用“AI 变革游戏开发领域”的态度上一直格外积极。公司首席执行官安德鲁・威尔逊曾在 2024 年 5 月的财报会议上向投资者表示：“我们将人工智能视为推动创意、创新以及玩家联结的强大加速器。”公司鼓励各部门员工 —— 从美术设计、质量检测，到市场营销和客户服务 —— 在日常工作流程中积极尝试使用 AI 工具。

articles.title: 专门陪骗子聊天的 AI 公司 Apate 拿下近千万美元融资，已累计消耗诈骗者 17 年时间
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据 TechCrunch 昨日报道，澳大利亚初创公司 Apate 成立于 2024 年，他们没有把 AI 用在提高工作效率，而是选择让 AI 和骗子“斗智斗勇”。基于悉尼麦考瑞大学的研究，Apate 部署了数千个伪装成无辜诈骗受害者的 AI 智能体。这些智能体可以接听诈骗电话、回复可疑信息和邮件、追踪钓鱼链接，并加入社交媒体群组以诱骗骗子。智能体可以假扮成各种各样的人，年龄、性别和口音各异，讲着各种语言，目的就是尽量多消耗骗子的时间。该公司表示，其智能体团队迄今为止在 250 万次对话中累计浪费了骗子 17 年的时间。更重要的是，对于 Apate 的客户群 —— 银行、电信公司、政府机构和公用事业公司 —— 来说，“卧底 AI 特工”可以让骗子透露一些通常只有在受害者被骗后才会知道的个人信息：银行账户、加密钱包、电话号码、恶意网站、他们冒充的品牌以及其他诈骗细节。随着 AI 的发展，骗子也能借用 AI 不断升级其骗术。2025 年，美国联邦调查局收到了超过 2.2 万起与 AI 相关的犯罪投诉，这些诈骗导致了约 8.93 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 59.86 亿元人民币）的损失。美国联邦调查局称诈骗者利用 AI 操控对话，并对名人、高管和可信人物的声音和形象进行深度伪造。有趣的是，Apate 的创意正是源自一个真实的诈骗电话。几年前，Apate 创始人兼首席执行官 Dali Kaafar 在一次家庭野餐时接到了一个陌生号码的电话。他意识到电话那边是骗子，于是决定装傻，硬生生耗了骗子 44 分钟时间。Kaafar 随后想到，那 44 分钟里骗子并没有打电话给真正的受害者，那么能否自动化这个流程？这一想法最终促成了 Kaafar 在麦考瑞大学的工作，他和同事们利用机器学习和自然语言处理技术揭露诈骗电话内容，并开发出了更好的检测和防范诈骗的方法。“大多数行业都是事后才补救的。电信公司会封锁号码，但骗子只会换新号码。银行会监控交易，但那时骗子已经联系到客户了。我们则会直接主动联系骗子，在其他人被骗之前获取信息，”Apate 联合创始人兼首席商务官 Brad Joffe 告诉 TechCrunch。“我们的 AI 智能体每天通过电话、消息、电子邮件和网络与成千上万的骗子沟通。我们为客户提供的是这些对话中产生的成果，以及他们能从中做些什么。”Joffe 表示，Apate 既会使用前沿模型，也会利用自身精细调优的模型来驱动智能体和分析。Apate 除了提供智能体服务，还可以为客户提供针对其终端用户或员工、品牌、产品等的诈骗情报和分析。客户甚至可以指派这些智能体执行特定任务，比如获取骗子的银行账户号码或加密钱包地址。其短信智能体可以搜索论坛、投资团体和社交平台，寻找潜在的诈骗活动，然后以虚假身份进入对话，揭露骗子的详细诈骗步骤。Apate 的客户包括澳大利亚联邦银行、TPG 电信，以及其他公用事业、电信公司和政府机构。Joffe 表示，TPG 已将近 59 万个电话转接给 Apate 的智能体，澳大利亚联邦银行公开报告的诈骗损失下降了 76%，一家未具名的澳大利亚银行也利用其外呼智能体破坏了 22 起诈骗活动。Apate 于今年 8 月筹集了 815 万美元（现汇率约合 5,462.9 万元人民币）的种子轮融资，该公司拥有 20 名员工，总筹集资金已接近 1,000 万美元（现汇率约合 6,703 万元人民币），计划将最新一轮资金投入产品和拓展国际业务，包括在伦敦开设办事处并在美国扩大影响力。Joffe 表示：“Apate 的名字来源于希腊神话中的欺骗女神，这与我们的工作非常契合。”

articles.title: 美国众议员提出《玩家权利法案》：玩家购买数字游戏应获得“真正所有权”
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据外媒 Techspot 报道，玩家购买数字游戏究竟是否真正拥有游戏的问题，终于进入美国联邦层面的立法讨论。近期美国众议员里奇 · 托雷斯提出《Power to the Players Act》（玩家权利法案），计划要求游戏厂商保障玩家对已购游戏的所有权，并在关闭在线服务器前提供离线游玩模式。不过，该提案目前仍处于早期阶段，具体实施细节及最终能否通过仍存在诸多不确定性。根据托雷斯公布的方案，该法案将要求美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）制定相关规则，确保消费者购买电子游戏后获得的是实际所有权，而非厂商可以随时撤销的使用许可，对于依赖在线服务器运行的游戏，厂商还必须在关闭服务器前提供离线模式。托雷斯表示，相应法案“旨在恢复游戏卡带和光盘时代的传统消费权益”，其援引即将停止销售和关闭服务器的《NBA 2K25》为例。这款游戏标准版上市价格为 70 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 469.2 元人民币），全明星版售价为 100 美元（现汇率约合 670.3 元人民币），曾是 2024 年美国最畅销游戏之一。不过本作将于 10 月 30 日从数字商店下架，并于 12 月 31 日关闭在线服务器，服务器关闭后，玩家购买游戏时所期待的部分在线模式也将随之无法使用。因此，托雷斯认为“如果一家公司只需拔掉插头就能收回一款游戏，那么这就不是购买，而是伪装成销售的租赁”。事实上，美国加利福尼亚州此前曾有一项类似提案《Protect Our Games Act》，相应提案曾试图要求游戏厂商在关闭服务器前至少提前 60 天通知玩家，并提供“离线模式、支持社区自建服务器或全额退款”等补救措施。不过，该法案在州参议院委员会审议时未能获得足够支持，最终以少于通过门槛 3 票的结果受阻。与加州方案主要关注游戏停服后的补救措施不同，托雷斯提出的《玩家权利法案》试图直接挑战数字游戏的许可模式。更值得注意的是，提案明确提及游戏转让权，这可能为数字游戏二手交易市场打开空间。目前，主流数字游戏平台普遍不允许玩家像转售实体光盘那样转售数字游戏，而美国法院此前通常认为，以许可形式提供的软件不适用允许转售已购商品的“首次销售原则”。不过，这项提案距离成为法律仍有很长的路要走。它目前尚未正式提交美国国会，同时绝大多数法案最终都无法进入全体议员表决阶段。此外，游戏发行商此前已经投入资源，反对范围更窄的相关立法，因此该提案未来可能面临来自行业的更大阻力。

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20665v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. articles.title: Evaluating Model Capabilities After Benchmark Saturation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20667v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rapid advances in AI capabilities are causing benchmarks to saturate. Once several models approach perfect scores, a benchmark loses its power to differentiate between them, and with it its utility for informing AI safety cases and frontier policies. Yet benchmark items produce far more information than the scores we typically extract from them: a full transcript of how each model solved the task. We investigate whether these transcripts can be used to assess model capabilities even after benchmark scores have saturated. articles.content:

Abstract: Reward-guided discrete diffusion enables test-time alignment with downstream objectives, but applying Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) guidance at every denoising step is computationally expensive. Active guidance steps require additional reward evaluations and, for gradient-based proposals, value-gradient computations. Sparse guidance reduces this cost by guiding only a subset of timesteps, but commonly used schedules are fixed heuristics whose effectiveness can vary substantially across tasks. We propose VISTA, a training-free method that automatically selects guided timesteps under a fixed budget. VISTA formulates sparse guidance as approximation of the ideal full-guidance probability path and derives an estimable upper bound on \(\ell_1\) path deviation. Abstract: Agents pair reasoning models with harnesses that organize model calls, execute tools, load skill instructions, and retain history in memory. Abstract: Correctness feedback suppresses the very evidence that specification-completeness auditing is designed to uncover: programs that satisfy a written contract but violate intended behavior. articles.title: Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields: Evidence-Grounded Selective Safety for Vision-Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20679v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Representation-based safety defenses for vision-language models (VLMs) often learn to separate harmful from benign inputs, but separation alone does not establish what a risk score means or when it should be trusted. We introduce Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields (CNRF), an evidence-grounded framework for selective VLM safety. CNRF constructs context-matched benign-harmful counterfactual pairs, uses their representation differences as capability-related risk directions, and estimates neighborhood support separately from risk. This separation prevents unfamiliarity from being conflated with harmfulness and enables selective intervention rather than blanket rejection. articles.title: IneqAgent: Agentic Inequality Proving in Lean with Symbolic Computation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20681v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Formal inequality proving requires mathematical reasoning and exact computation, often connected through intermediate lemmas and goal reformulations. We introduce IneqAgent, an agentic framework combining LLM reasoning with symbolic computation for inequality proving in Lean4. Lemma-level Monte Carlo Tree Search coordinates lemma construction, goal reformulation, and symbolic backend selection. Complementary sum-of-squares, Bernstein, and successive difference-substitution backends produce exact certificates for local Lean proof generation. The agent integrates these proofs with LLM-generated steps and uses Lean feedback to construct complete proofs checked against the original theorem statements. On four benchmarks, IneqAgent with DeepSeek-V4-Flash solves 175 of 186 problems (94.09%), achieving the highest overall success rate among the evaluated methods. articles.title: L2G-SR: Learning to Guide LLM-based Symbolic Regression
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20685v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic regression searches for an equation that explains observed data. Numerical error is commonly used to guide the search, but it alone can favor an accurate surrogate over a candidate with the right structure. We propose L2G-SR, a framework for LLM-based symbolic regression that guides search with a learned structural verifier. We construct structural supervision signal using tree edit distance (TED), accounting for commutative operators and alternative expression forms. A verifier first aligns numerical observations with the formulas, then learns to score a candidate's structural similarity to the target formula. At search time, the target formula is hidden and the verifier complements numerical error in parent selection. An analyst then uses verifier feedback and diagnostic tools to propose revisions, which a generator converts into refined expressions. Abstract: This paper challenges the understanding capabilities of existing AI paradigms and emerging world models by asking a fundamental question: How quickly can reality change before an intelligent system can no longer reliably perceive, reason, and act? Abstract: In LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), a local mistake can propagate as other agents build on it, turning a correctable error into a failed task. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20782v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The closed world asks AI for specialized competence and lets it manufacture the iid data its theory assumes: a fixed criterion licenses collecting examples until the task is covered. The open world asks for versatility --- taking up tasks a machine was not built for, from few examples and with little prior from a human designer --- and offers data that is grouped, not shuffled. Its tasks are not known in advance, so a machine must do inference-time learning (1st requirement). Modeling tasks as sharing latent factors and decomposing the training objective, we derive two more: a *rich representation*, retaining more than iid generalization requires, and a predictive disentanglement that aligns inputs and outputs into matched low-dimensional groups. Abstract: Multi-modal agents have made significant progress in interacting with open worlds. However, their ability to self-evolve remains limited. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20805v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A reasoning trace retained at answer time plays two roles: it can raise accuracy, and it can compete with the current evidence when the two disagree. We disentangle these roles by crossing verified evidence versions with the traces generated from each and answering from the same traces and evidence under two configurations: continuation of the model's own thinking and a separate answer call. Across three model families (gpt-oss, Gemma4, Qwen3) on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, the separate call raises evidence-following over continuation by 29.9 to 60.6 points. On the same pairs, removing the trace lowers accuracy by similar amounts under both configurations. Abstract: A self-improving agent has to decide which new skills to keep, and in practice it keeps whatever earns a high reward, convinces a judge model, or compresses its library, even when the skill is wrong. That is fine until the answers have to be exactly right: over a table of transactions, a total is either right or wrong. We ask a harder question: can an agent grow what it can compute with no reward, no judge, and no answer key, and still be exactly right? The inner loop answers new questions only when two independently written expressions agree on every record. Abstract: Evaluator-guided reasoning presents a local control problem at every step: trust the current answer, return a fallback, or spend more inference. A local action-gap analysis characterizes when score errors can change a decision, while an expected regret bound accounts for errors along the realized expansion path. Guided by this analysis, we learn and calibrate action-specific confidence estimates, with local uncertainty penalties for ambiguous decisions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20845v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Skill-policy co-evolution, in which an agent's policy model and its skill bank improve each other during training, is a promising paradigm for self-improving agents. Current evaluations score the co-evolved policy on the final bank it trained with (the delivered bank). After deployment, however, skills may be rewritten, added or removed more frequently than the policy model is retrained, leaving the policy to operate on a drifted skill bank that neither the training objective nor existing evaluation protocols address. In this paper, we first establish, through theoretical and empirical analysis, that the fragility hidden by this blind spot is not incidental. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20867v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a general declarative framework for anticipatory reasoning about interactive motion in complex dynamic environments. Our focus is on (explainable) anticipatory space-time mental model formation at a semantic level to heuristically guide low-level motion computation. Our method is hybrid, modular and elaboration tolerant integrating: 1) An ASP model characterising the dynamics of interactive motion trajectories; 2) Semantically-guided prediction for deriving `branching trajectory futures'; and 3) An energy-based {optimisation} model to evaluate, rank and filter anticipations. We evaluate with the Argoverse 2 benchmark, where each anticipated trajectory carries an explicit, inspectable event-level hypothesis, unlike end-to-end stochastic prediction.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20921v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most debate about releasing capable AI systems treats the choice as binary: keep the model behind an API, or publish the weights. That framing runs together two separate decisions. One is how capable a system may become. The other is who may obtain a given capability, and on what terms. This paper is about the second decision. We propose a Multi-Tiered AI Accessibility Model (MAIAM) that sorts access by purpose, safety, and capability instead of by release artifact. Tier 1, AI for Learning, is broadly accessible and deliberately capability-bounded. Tier 2, AI for Exploration, serves research and development under registration, identity, and usage controls that tighten as capability rises. Tier 3, Full-Scale Frontier AI, is available only through structured, recorded, and accountable access. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20922v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Compositional structure is pervasive in nature and across scales: atoms combine into molecules, molecules into cells, and cells into organisms, while further compositional hierarchies appear within each level. More broadly, compositionality, the reuse and recombination of parts into novel structures, is a fundamental source of interesting complexity in both natural and artificial systems. Yet despite its importance, and despite our apparent ease in recognizing it, mathematical accounts capturing what we intuitively mean by compositional structure remain limited. Here, we fill this gap by formalizing a simple idea: compositional structure emerges when parts, considered together, reveal shared structure that is not captured when those parts are modeled separately. Abstract: Research on deceptive alignment is becoming increasingly urgent as frontier-model capabilities advance and their risk of causing catastrophic harm increases. Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is credited with gains beyond the domain its rewards check, such as higher MMLU accuracy after training on mathematics. Abstract: Global streamflow forecasting supports flood preparedness, yet data-driven models trained on reanalysis lose skill when driven by operational forecasts, increasingly so with lead time. AIFL addresses this shift with a two-stage transfer-learning recipe and a deterministic LSTM, but it feeds one forecast lead time into the whole input window and gives no uncertainty. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20680v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are typically trained on hundreds of millions to billions of activation tokens, yet little work has tested whether this scale is necessary. A small Transformer uses this global context and earlier tokens within the block to predict the next token. Abstract: Multi-head latent attention (MLA) compresses the content of a key-value cache into a shared latent per token, making low-bit storage attractive for long-context inference. At two bits, errors in this representation perturb both attention matching and value readout, with effects that depend on error direction and reconstruction scale. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20687v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Residual context is key to unlocking the speed-quality Pareto frontier of diffusion language models (DLMs) by carrying forward predictive distributions across denoising steps. ORL learns from model-induced residual trajectories on the fly and introduces an entropy-contraction objective that sharpens predictions as the model revisits its own predictions. Abstract: Quantile forecasts summarize uncertainty at each future time step, while diffusion forecasters represent it through sampled future trajectories. We study how predicted quantiles can serve as distributional controls for diffusion forecasting. Specifically, we investigate how the mechanism of quantile integration affects its effectiveness in guiding a pretrained diffusion forecaster. We instantiate this approach as Control-TS, which learns a quantile-control pathway while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen. Across eight benchmarks, Control-TS consistently improves the backbone's CRPS, achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art forecasting models, and retains its gains in capacity-matched comparisons. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20795v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Understanding why listeners enjoy music is difficult because the experience is subjective and changes as a piece unfolds. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive way to study neural responses during listening, yet earlier work has mostly treated music emotion as a categorical label or relied on black-box models. We formulate enjoyment prediction as a regression problem on the public MUSIN-G dataset, which contains 128-channel EEG from 20 listeners together with song-level enjoyment ratings. Six deep learning models were compared under a participant-wise protocol, in which 15 listeners were used for training and validation and 5 were held out for testing. DeepConvNet, CNN-LSTM and GNN-CNN reached the lowest mean absolute error (0.97 to 0.99 on the 1 to 5 scale), while the temporal convolutional network (TCN) had the highest Pearson correlation with the ratings (r = 0.21). articles.title: DeepUnfolding_Agent: A Classical_Quantum Adaptive Control API
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20615v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adaptive optimization workflows in machine learning, federated learning, quantum machine learning, and hybrid classical quantum systems often embed controller logic directly inside task specific training scripts. This coupling limits reuse, reproducibility, safety validation, and fair comparison across execution environments. This paper presents DeepUnfolding Agent, a schema-driven FastAPI platform that exposes deep unfolded adaptive control as an external software service. External executors register a strategy schema, submit round-level diagnostic variables, receive schema-bounded control actions, execute one optimization round, and return feedback for controller update. articles.title: PRISM: PRIvileged Sibling-guided Multi-Agent Topology Design
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20628v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) based on large language models (LLMs) have become a powerful way to address complex problems, and their effectiveness depends critically on the collaboration topology that decides which agents participate and how they communicate. Recent work learns to generate this topology from the task query, fitting the generator to corpora of execution-verified graphs. The post-training method for such generators remains a limitation: a corpus lists the graphs that solved a query but never ranks them, leaving continued supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with no per-query preference to exploit. Without such a preference, the generator drifts toward the topologies the corpus contains most often rather than those that suit each query, so a gain on one task can come at a cost on another. articles.title: A Large-Scale Dataset for Multi-Class Financial News Classification in Brazilian Portuguese
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20630v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The development of Financial Natural Language Processing (NLP) systems for Brazilian Portuguese is hindered by the scarcity of domain-specific datasets. To address this, we present a large-scale corpus of approximately 160,000 Brazilian Portuguese financial news articles collected from web sources. To establish initial benchmarks for a weakly supervised multi-class classification approach based on semantic similarity, we annotated subsets of this corpus both manually and using a Large Language Model (LLM). We evaluated three similarity-based methods -- cosine similarity, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and FAISS-based nearest-neighbor search -- using multilingual semantic embeddings. Our experiments reveal that the task is highly sensitive to label quality and class distribution. articles.title: Real-time Chatbot Romance Scam Detection in Stage Classification
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20631v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Romance scam has become a serious problem via social media, and the improvement of artificial intelligence enable to fake identify easily. In the study, a chatbot has developed to detect romance scam in real-time through Line Messaging API. Using the seven stage theories in the social science field, the stages of romance scam can be detected through large language model. In addition, once a romance scam is detected, the chatbot provides explanations of the stage and prevention advices through large language model. The contribution of the work provides a practical application, and can be used in real scenario for reducing the risk of romance scam.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20632v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern healthcare generates increasingly complex medical reports that challenge clinical professionals in terms of time and interpretive burden. Manual review processes are slow, error-prone, and difficult to scale. This paper presents MeddeX, a Medical Report Analyzer that combines a QLoRA fine-tuned LLaMA-3 (8B) model with Retrieval-Augmented Gen eration (RAG) and a multimodal Gemini Vision layer to deliver accurate, concise, and evidence-backed summaries of medical documents. The system handles text-native PDFs, scanned image based PDFs, and direct radiological images through an intelligent hybrid extraction pipeline that includes a novel garbage-text detection mechanism for corrupted and UTF-16-encoded doc uments. articles.title: Context Injection and Long-Horizon Reliability: Separating Duplicate Recognition, Local Processing, and Counter Tracking
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20633v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon failures of language models are usually measured as end-task success or as a horizon length. We instead score, step by step, three components of a 400-step ledger task in which every step is easy in isolation and the model's own answers are re-injected into its context: recognising a record already seen 5 to 300 steps earlier, processing the current record locally, and writing a counter incremented at every step. On Qwen3-8B (non-thinking, 20 seeds, replicated on a second machine and backend), with every step scored component by component, two results hold. First, duplicate-recognition errors rise late in the episode -- from 0.0019 to 0.011 per step at risk across step 200 -- while the counter makes no error in 8,000 steps and local processing is descriptively stable; the rise combines long-distance recall errors and rising false alarms. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20634v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation asks one question at volume: does this evidence support this claim? The answer is one bit, yet most pipelines obtain it from a text generator and pay generation prices for the prose wrapped around it. We compare a non-generative decision model, which returns a typed value from a declared enumeration together with a native probability and no text, against a frontier LLM configured as an engineer would deploy it for binary classification. Both answer the same 495 human-labelled claims from LLM-AggreFact, so every comparison is within-item. We report three things. First, the two systems are statistically indistinguishable on the metric this task is conventionally scored by, a paired difference of -0.56 points, Jev minus Astra, at a 187-fold cost difference. articles.title: Exploring the Design Space of Permutation Diffusion LLMs
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20635v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Permutation generation with language models requires both text-conditioned ranking and a global one-to-one assignment between candidates and output positions. We study this problem through three diffusion-LLM parameterizations: hard-assignment prediction over shuffled candidate-index sequences, soft-assignment prediction over doubly stochastic matrices, and direct ordering-score prediction followed by sorting. The three families place permutation constraints at different stages of prediction and decoding and therefore support different training objectives and sampling procedures. We evaluate these designs on recommendation reranking across three Amazon domains with candidate sets of size 10 and 20. articles.title: AbridgeKV: Compressing Long Reasoning into the KV Cache of Learned Pause Tokens
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20641v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long chain-of-thought decoding is memory-bound: the KV cache of the generated tokens grows linearly with the test-time compute being spent. Evicting cache entries does not fix this, because a model never trained on a cache with entries removed generates longer, often up to the length limit. We instead train the model to compress its own output. AbridgeKV compresses each completed block of generated text into the KV entries of a few learned pause tokens. These are extra input tokens with trained embeddings that produce no output. Once the pause tokens have encoded the block, AbridgeKV frees the block's original cache; subsequent tokens attend to the pause tokens' KV entries in its place. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20642v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent latent reasoning methods move beyond discrete Chain-of-Thought (CoT) by replacing sampled tokens with continuous soft embeddings or hidden states, enabling richer intermediate representations and preserving alternative reasoning paths. However, the need for latent reasoning varies across decoding steps: confident predictions favor discrete commitment, whereas ambiguous steps benefit from preserving multiple plausible alternatives. Existing approaches typically handle this variation through either global soft activation or hard switching based on uncertainty thresholds, treating latent intervention as an all-or-nothing decision rather than continuously adapting its strength. articles.title: Does Personalization Break Trust? Open-Set Rejection Calibration Under Few-Shot On-Device Intent Adaptation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20652v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Always-on virtual assistants increasingly personalize on-device to new user-specific commands via few-shot fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA), but this adaptation is evaluated almost exclusively on whether it learns the new commands, not on whether the assistant can still recognize an input that matches none of its intents - the out-of-scope (OOS) rejection problem. We show that naive few-shot LoRA personalization degrades OOS-rejection AUROC (area under the ROC curve) on every one of five public intent-classification benchmarks (mean drop $0.055$--$0.258$, five seeds each), while in-scope accuracy is preserved. A scorer-invariant check shows part of this drop is an artifact of the standard confidence scorer's own miscalibration under adaptation, though a smaller, genuine effect remains under any scorer; we trace it to a measurable shrinkage of the embedding margin around known-intent regions (pooled Spearman rho=0.61$). articles.title: Reference-Guided Turn-Taking Style Transfer for Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20763v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Full-duplex spoken language models decide at every frame whether to take the floor, defining a conversational personality -- yet each set of weights encodes exactly one, which human speakers bracket rather than share. Existing controls mostly act from outside; none identifies the quantity that sets how much the model speaks. We identify it: a single late-layer residual-stream direction, the initiative vector, extracted from the model's own conversations without training or annotation. The same direction reads the decision, anticipating onsets up to 800 ms ahead, and shifts it: scaled during generation, it moves speech ratio from 6-12% to 42-61% (no steering: 21-30%), consistently across conversations, weights, and corpora. articles.title: Verdict: Encode Once, Decide Many
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20778v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automating organizational work means answering many small typed questions about one piece of state (does this email need a reply, how urgent is it, who owns it) with probabilities good enough to act on without a human. The open typed-decision model we compare against, like a standard cross-encoder, answers each question with a separate pass over the input. We present Verdict-MQ, an open encoder that reads a case once and answers all of its questions: given identical retained state tokens after truncation (verified on every reported case), a structured attention mask makes the state encoding independent of the questions, keeps questions from influencing each other, and makes option order irrelevant by construction. articles.title: APRiL: An Open-ended Benchmark for Chinese Social Awareness in Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20785v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in social interactions, where appropriate responses require recognizing implicit cues, inferring mental states, identifying conflicts, and considering potential consequences. However, existing benchmarks often focus on specific social abilities, constrained task formats, or particular interaction settings, offering limited coverage of social awareness across diverse contexts. To address this gap, we introduce APRiL, an open-ended benchmark for Chinese social awareness with instance-specific rubrics. APRiL contains 2,196 Social Awareness Evaluation Instances across six categories and two complementary tasks: Social Scenario Analysis evaluates models' understanding of social cues, mental states, and conflict structures, while Socially Aware Response assesses whether they can translate this understanding into appropriate, natural responses. articles.title: PRISM: Transfer and Limits of Activation Interventions in Tool-Calling Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20808v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent literature shows that unsafe tool calls can often accompany textual refusals in language models. To investigate this hidden vulnerability, we introduce PRISM, a framework for evaluating the transfer of activation interventions across precision, languages, and scales. Our findings demonstrate that leveraging lower-resource settings (specifically quantized NF4 labels and cross-lingual transfer) offers a robust pathway to expose and improve model alignment. Notably, using behavioral labels from an NF4 copy enables stable intervention estimation even with very few scenarios. Furthermore, these alignment improvements transfer effectively across languages: five-language NF4-supervised directions successfully transfer to held-out Arabic, reducing unsafe violations in Llama-3.1-8B by 21.95 percentage points without target-language tuning. articles.title: Wolof-Adapted Industry-Ready Open-Weight Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20824v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Wolof is spoken by 23M people, mostly in Senegal, but remains weakly supported by open-weight language models, while API models raise cost, governance, and sovereignty constraints for local deployments. In this paper, we present 0.6B-14B open-weight models adapted to Wolof through instruction tuning, preference alignment, and model merging. After presenting the pipeline and data, extensive experiments on 63~public and in-house tasks show good performance on Wolof understanding and generation while remaining effective on other languages and cross-lingual skills, with the 8B and 14B models being particularly competitive with substantially larger commercial systems. The models are currently being evaluated in internal customer-care pilots and are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/collections/Orange/wolof-lm .

articles.title: CoTranslator: Reverse to Forward Chain-of-Thought Translator for Reasoning Distillation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20828v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning distillation requires chain-of-thought (CoT) data with correct answers, but obtaining such data efficiently remains challenging. Forward CoT generation (FCG) followed by rejection sampling (RS) produces verified, question-only responses, yet may require many teacher calls for difficult problems. Reverse CoT generation (RCG) is cheaper because it conditions on the known answer, but access to this answer can lead to post-hoc rationalization and a mismatch with the student's answer-free inference setting. We propose CoTranslator, which learns to translate reverse CoT responses toward the distribution of verified forward responses. Trained on a small set of paired reverse and rejection-sampled forward responses, it supports large-scale generation and verification of student training data. Across six student models evaluated on six mathematics benchmarks, CoTranslator improves average accuracy over semantic suppression by up to $5.8

articles.title: PEDBench: Can Speech Models Detect Phonetic Errors?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20830v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Phonetic error detection (PED) aims to identify phoneme-level substitutions, deletions, and insertions and is essential for educational and clinical speech assessment and intervention. Despite recent advances in speech models for phoneme recognition, their ability to reliably detect fine-grained phonetic errors remains unclear because of a lack of high-quality evaluation data. To address this gap, we introduce PEDBench, the first PED benchmark spanning a continuum from natural to controlled speech. It comprises real-world recordings of spoken errors made by children (N=334), scripted error productions by human actors (N=1,188), and synthetic error productions generated using phone-conditioned text-to-speech (N=1,083). All phonetic annotations were transcribed and verified by two phonetically trained annotators. articles.title: Does Morphological Correctness Matter for Tokenization? A Scrambled Control Study in Tagalog
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20859v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Typology-aware tokenizers are motivated by the claim that segmentation which respects morpheme boundaries preserves information that frequency-driven segmentation destroys. Studies routinely establish that it helps while assuming the boundaries must be linguistically correct. We separate them. Tagalog marks voice with infixes (s-um-ulat 'wrote', s-in-ulat 'was written'), so the root is not contiguous and no sequence of BPE merges can recover it. We build MorphAustro-Tok, a tokenizer that emits the root as a contiguous unit followed by a positional infix token, and compare it against a corpus-matched BPE baseline and, at two of three fertility levels, against a scrambled-morpheme control that preserves morph count, invertibility and per-type consistency while randomising the pseudo-infix. articles.title: Prune the Summary, Not the History: Source-Judged Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20927v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents rely on context compaction: when the interaction history outgrows the context window, a compressor replaces it with a natural-language summary. We show that these summaries contain more than a record of what happened. Compaction prompts ask for decisions and next steps, so each summary mixes facts established by the environment with reasoning written by the compressor, and the agent cannot tell the two apart afterwards. In an analysis of a widely used structured compressor, 83% of failed runs trace back to an action that carries out a specific summary entry, most of which no environment output supports. We propose Source-Judged Compaction (SJC), a training-free post-processing step that scores each summary entry for whether it has a source in the environment outputs or the previous summary, and removes the entries that do not. articles.title: BD-HazardVLM: Probing Vision-Language Models for Latent Defensive-Driving Hazards in Bangladesh Road Scenes
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20627v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language models are increasingly used for driving-scene understanding, yet their defensive reasoning under weakly structured Global South traffic remains unclear. We introduce BD-HazardVLM, a diagnostic benchmark of 500 Bangladesh road-scene images, comprising 375 from RSUD20K and 125 from TFP-BD, annotated for hazard presence, primary hazard category, risk timing, severity, defensive actions, visible evidence, and hallucination- and Western-road-bias traps. We evaluate Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-8B, and MiniCPM-V-4.6 using a shared zero-shot task definition and structured output schema. Binary hazard-presence accuracy ranges from 88.0 percent to 89.2 percent, essentially matching the 89.0 percent majority-class baseline. Fine-grained reasoning is substantially weaker: category accuracy remains below 40 percent, risk-timing accuracy ranges from 1.6 percent to 12.4 percent, and exact defensive-action matching remains below 2 percent.

articles.title: Towards automatic digital garment assembly
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20651v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Creating digital garments from existing two-dimensional patterns remains a time-consuming process. Although patterns are widely available in digital form, their assembly in garment CAD software involves manual definition of sewing operations and arrangement of the pattern panels for drape simulation. We present two learning-based approaches that automate both tasks using the 2D vector pattern as their sole input. Our automatic sewing model operates at the segment level, leveraging a Transformer encoder with multiple prediction heads. Our novel architecture supports many-to-many, ordered segment correspondences, as well as hems, overlapping seams needed for multilayer garments, and construction properties such as seam allowances and stitch types, required for the finished virtual garment but neglected by previous methods. articles.title: Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20693v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. Existing benchmarks assess selected geometric properties or use vision-language models to judge memory and consistency, leaving systematic 3D evaluation underexplored. We introduce Orbia, the first benchmark dedicated to a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of 3D consistency in interactive world models. Through controlled exploration and revisit, we organize the evaluation into three dimensions: input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency. articles.title: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans interpret multimodal observations of the world and forecast how it will evolve. Recent multimodal generative systems have demonstrated similar capabilities: they can integrate multimodal context and synthesize visual outputs that depict changes in the world. To characterize this emerging trajectory, we organize model capabilities into a four-level hierarchy and discover that higher-level tasks remain relatively underexplored despite model progress. To bridge this gap, we explore model performance on multi-step world state prediction, a high-level task that requires models to forecast successive future world states from multimodal observations and diverse references. Such a task requires models to possess entangled understanding and generation capabilities, as well as extensive world knowledge to translate human action sequences, physical transformations, and abstract visual reasoning into coherent visual outputs. articles.title: Purify Before You Align: Improving Representation Alignment for Diffusion Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20761v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Representation alignment improves and accelerates diffusion training by encouraging intermediate features to match a pretrained visual encoder. However, standard alignment matches pretrained representations without distinguishing what information may be more useful for generation. We introduce local appearance purification (LAP), which improves generation quality and makes encoders such as MAE more effective alignment targets by removing locally predictable content and aligning to the residual. LAP modifies only the alignment target, and requires no changes to diffusion training or inference. Abstract: Image-to-text (I2T) understanding and text-to-image (T2I) generation are dual tasks in unified multimodal models (UMMs). Reconstructive post-training couples these tasks, but existing reconstruction-based methods remain perception-centric and provide limited supervision for reasoning about structure, intent, and transformation. Given an original image and an editing instruction, the UMM first reasons about what and how to edit and describes the target state, then generates the corresponding target image conditioned on this understanding output. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20794v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent reinforcement learning approaches have improved visual text generation, yet generated images still suffer from incorrect wording and malformed glyphs. We identify two coupled limitations: recognition-based rewards often overlook visible glyph defects, while whole-image scalar feedback obscures the uneven quality of individual text regions. These limitations motivate our central principle: $\textit{Blame errant words, not the canvas}$, to effectively preserve local quality distinctions. First, we introduce $\mathbf{TextDART}$, a defect-aware region-targeted reward model that localizes individual text regions and independently evaluates their semantic correctness and glyph quality, providing fine-grained, region-precise feedback. Abstract: Unified multimodal generation covers discrete, continuous, and hybrid paradigms. Discrete approaches with single-codebook visual tokenizers align naturally with text modeling but have limited representational capacity. Continuous and hybrid approaches retain richer visual representations, but they model text and images in heterogeneous spaces with different training objectives, potentially introducing optimization conflicts between modalities with misaligned representation spaces. These choices expose a central question: how to efficiently model high-capacity visual representations alongside textual content in a shared optimization space within a single backbone. Abstract: Map generation tasks feature extensive non-structural vectorized data (e.g., points, polylines, and polygons) and thus pose significant challenges to common pixel-wise generative models. For training MARS, we collected to our knowledge the largest multi-class map extraction dataset totaling 3.4M examples, which we call MAP-3M. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20852v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Negation is a fundamental aspect of language understanding and it is important vision-language models (VLMs) are able to process it effectively. We investigate how VLMs process negation by analysing attention patterns of different models. We draw comparisons between human gaze and attention in models when processing affirmative vs negated statements. We compare object level model attention to human eye-fixations in both binary and multary settings, evaluating with both synthetic and realistic datasets. We find models generally do not follow human-like attention patterns when resolving negation, suggesting they rely on mechanisms outside of attention. While layerwise analysis shows that PaliGemma2-3B shifts object attention to the alternative under negation, our headwise ablations suggest this is a byproduct rather than a negation processing mechanism. Abstract: Insect-induced defoliation threatens grapevine health and yield, yet severity assessment relies on subjective manual scouting. We developed DefoliationCAM (D-CAM), a solar-powered edge AI system that estimates canopy defoliation and transmits results via LoRa to a web dashboard. The pipeline uses YOLOX-Nano to localize grapevine cordons in 4K images and a MobileNet-based classifier with lightweight channel attention to classify 320 x 320 pixel patches. The 29,674 field-collected patches were labeled as background or one of four damage levels: no to negligible, mild, moderate, and severe. Merging moderate and severe classes reduced the class imbalance ratio from approximately 40:1 to 8.8:1. Synthetic augmentation increased macro-F1 from 0.768 to 0.838. Abstract: While foundation models and vision transformers (ViTs) have redefined visual representations, current active learning (AL) strategies for these backbones largely operate at the patch or region level, where annotation requirements remain high due to extensive pixel labeling. Abstract: Occupancy predictors rely on large persistent banks of Gaussians or learned queries whose size is fixed by hand. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20964v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing long-document QA benchmarks rarely combine large-scale human-authored questions with detailed visual evidence annotations, limiting diagnosis of evidence localization and interpretation failures. We present VELD-QA, a large-scale benchmark for Visual Evidence grounding and question answering in Long Documents. It contains 15,000 fully human-authored question-answer pairs across 5,859 real-world PDFs totaling 372,445 pages, balancing chart, table, and complex-layout tasks. Human annotations identify supporting pages and evidence elements and describe cited visual content, enabling separate retrieval and interpretation evaluation. We evaluate nine vision-language models under four evidence settings and seven retrieval-augmented and agentic systems. Abstract: Geo-foundation models (GFMs) are typically evaluated by downstream task predictive performance, revealing little about which physical features they are sensitive to or use in prediction. Abstract: Spatial agents have access to reconstruction and segmentation tools, yet inconsistent predictions and fragmented object identities can prevent their outputs from becoming reliable 3D scene information. Abstract: Diffusion models are notoriously expensive to train, requiring large-scale datasets to learn how to gradually reverse the noise from images over multiple small denoising steps. Abstract: Vehicles that lose control at the handling limit through icing, hydroplaning, or an abrupt evasive maneuver fall outside the operating envelope of production safety systems such as electronic stability control, which focus on preventing instability rather than recovering from it. Abstract: Satisfying safety constraints for systems with second-order dynamics is challenging because a position constraint may require infeasible deceleration. Higher-order control barrier functions (CBFs) provide an approach for expressing safety conditions for such systems but feasibility depends on the system dynamics and available control authority. We develop a constructive approach for designing feasible safety constraints for second-order control-affine systems. Starting from a signed distance function (SDF), we construct collision-free spheres, i.e., bubbles, in position space, and use their quadratic geometry and overlap to construct a velocity-dependent safety constraint. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20901v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Task-Oriented Grasping (TOG) has emerged as an important skill for purposeful robotic manipulation. Given the task of using a knife to "slice bread," a robot must choose to grasp from the handle, whereas for "hand[ing] the knife over," it is preferable for the handle to remain unobstructed for safe handoff. To that end, we present TGrasp6D, a vision-language based approach for generating task-oriented 6DoF grasps in a zero-shot manner. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robust adaptive control is vital for keeping robots safe while actively reducing uncertainty in unfamiliar settings. However, traditional methods are often conservative since they fail to account for guaranteed future parameter learning during planning and struggle to scale to high-dimensional systems. In this work, we present A-SLS, a learning-aware robust adaptive model predictive control (RAMPC) framework based on system-level synthesis. A-SLS forecasts future parameter uncertainty and preserves correlations between process disturbances, parameter error, and estimate updates to construct tight, guaranteed reachable sets that account for future information gain. We also develop a GPU-accelerated A-SLS solver to enable real-time performance. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20936v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generating dynamically feasible motions for legged and manipulating robots requires solving a large, nonlinear, non-convex optimal control problem (OCP) in which contact wrenches must satisfy friction-cone constraints throughout the motion, not only at isolated instants. articles.title: When a robot can trust reversing wind to find an odour source
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A wind-derived heading can guide a robot towards an odour source even after the wind reverses, but its reliability depends on the plume's transport history. On a quadruped initially facing the source, holding the initial heading reached it in every reversing-wind trial, whereas comparison controllers never settled there. An exact geometric condition links heading correctness to net odour transport, and simulations separate sensing error from departures from nominal flow. Where the alternating wind directions are too close for reversal alone to produce wrong-side headings, the wrong-side rate rises from 1.0% under uniform transport to 4.7% in a stochastic flow. Re-acquiring headings from new odour contact improves simulated search when contact is intermittent. These results identify distinct requirements for wind-guided search: a heading supported by the transport geometry and sufficient intermittent contact to replace it.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Passive human videos of everyday activity offer robots access to a massive amount of human experience without requiring a demonstration for each task. However, using this experience requires recovering knowledge from unstructured video recordings and adapting it to a different body (i.e., the robot). To overcome these challenges, we present mobile code-as-policy (MoCaP), an agentic framework that turns passive human video recordings into guidance for an end-to-end mobile manipulation policy. MoCaP extracts spatial memory and cues of how people prepare to interact with objects, which inform navigation and the search for a manipulation-ready configuration. Guided by passive human experience and current observations, MoCaP uses a closed-loop code-as-policy to coordinate planning and tool use primitives to solve motions under the robot's geometry and kinematic constraints. articles.title: Slip-Induced Fall Suppression During Cornering for a Remotely Operated Motorcycle with a Rear-Wheel-Swing Mechanism
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.21089v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Slip-induced falls when riding motorcycles are difficult to avoid even for expert riders and represent a major cause of single-vehicle accidents. Despite their prevalence, no practical solution has yet been proposed to suppress this phenomenon. We previously introduced a motorcycle model applicable to systems with both front- and rear- wheel steering. In this paper, we extend that model and formulate the suppression of slip-induced falls as an optimization problem that distributes assistive control inputs according to vehicle speed and road surface conditions. To evaluate the proposed method, we developed a remotely operated motorcycle and conducted experiments under two scenarios: slalom driving on a low-friction surface at 5.5 m/s, and turning maneuvers on synthetic ice to simulate driving over manholes on rainy days. The results demonstrate that our approach successfully suppresses falls under these challenging conditions.

articles.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
articles.content: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.

articles.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
articles.content: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder. The on-demand query formulation enables flexible spatial sampling, and our proposed continuous-time queries further provide temporal flexibility. To strengthen geometric knowledge, we propose a straightforward plug-in solution by incorporating a pretrained video-depth LoRA as a frozen geometry prior, improving overall performance without adding extra trainable parameters. Gen4P achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on tasks of 3D point tracking, video depth and camera pose estimation. Qualitative results on in-the-wild videos illustrate its capability of tracking complex motion while maintaining the delicate structure. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of video generative pretraining for unified 4D perception. See https://gen4p.github.io for more visual results.

articles.title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
articles.content: Token merging has emerged as an effective training-free strategy for accelerating diffusion models by reducing redundant token computation while minimizing generation degradation. A key challenge is determining which tokens can be safely merged and which should be preserved for subsequent computation. Existing method addresses this by preserving prompt-aligned foreground regions, thereby protecting semantically relevant structures. However, this text-relevance criterion overlooks background objects, local details that are not explicitly mentioned in the prompt, leading to degraded structural coherence. In this work, we propose Dynamics-aware Token Merging (DaTMe), a training-free framework that grounds token merging in the underlying diffusion dynamics. Our key insight is that token importance should reflect whether a token remains unresolved during denoising and whether it carries structural information. To this end, DaTMe constructs a dynamics- aware importance map from the Tweedie denoised estimate. The map combines a temporal signal, measuring inter-step changes in the predicted clean image, with a structural signal, capturing local high-frequency content such as boundaries and fine details. Using this map, DaTMe adaptively assigns tokens into merging roles under a given compression ratio: important tokens are preserved as anchors, while tokens that are both temporally stabilized and structurally homogeneous are selected as safe merge candidates. Experiments on PixArt-a and FLUX demonstrate that DaTMe maintains visual fidelity across the entire image, highlighting diffusion dynamics as an effective token-level merging decision in efficient generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/SeungJuCha/DaTMe.

articles.title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers
articles.content: Diffusion and flow models generate a sample over iterative steps, each a full pass through a large network, and that pass dominates generation cost. Training-free caching accelerates them by reusing activations from recent evaluations instead of recomputing them. Dynamic caching methods decide when to refresh by accumulating a cheap probe of the network input into a staleness signal and spending a fresh evaluation once it crosses a threshold. They perform hard caching: the signal is a binary switch between refresh and reuse, and every step, fresh or cached, advances by the prescribed step size. We observe that the signal carries much more than this switch. How far it sits below the threshold, its headroom, predicts the error induced by reuse. We propose SoftCache, which performs soft caching: instead of a binary switch, the headroom sets how far each cached step goes. Where the headroom is large, the sampler jumps past several scheduled nodes, and as a refresh nears, its steps shrink back toward the original step. These adaptive jumps may land between the scheduled nodes, taking the sampler off its fixed grid. SoftCache requires no training and adds no per-backbone settings: on FLUX for images and on HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 for video, at speedups from $3.5\times$ to $6.9\times$, it is ahead of every baseline on all four fidelity metrics.

articles.title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies
articles.content: Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience. We present Value as Memory (VaM), a framework that addresses these challenges through value caching and online real-world reinforcement learning (RL). Value caching conditions actions on recent value predictions as task-progress memory, while online updates enable timely policy improvement by combining offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation. As a result, VaM transitions from offline RL warmup to online autonomous learning with sparse rewards. Across long-horizon tasks involving deformable objects and contact-rich manipulation, VaM yields a mean absolute success-rate gain of $29.4\%$ with value caching, while achieving a $32.8\%$ gain with online autonomous learning over matched offline training. The evaluated online schedule performs $8\times$ as many policy iterations under the same gradient-step budget, with more than $2\times$ lower recorded time per gradient step with concurrent data collection and training.

articles.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
articles.content: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps -- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic -- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off for modular inversion. These results open the door for evaluator-guided LLM co-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation.

articles.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
articles.content: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.
